esp32dev.name: ESP32 DevKitC V4
esp32dev.subtitle: Wi-Fi / Bluetooth development board
esp32dev.description: A miniature controller board that connects to a network. It combines an ESP32 module, a USB-to-UART bridge, power circuitry, and pin headers so programming can begin over a computer connection.
esp32dev.tip: The silver shield covers the wireless module; the meandering copper trace at the board edge is the antenna. Keep large metal objects away from the antenna.
pinNotes: Programmable inputs and outputs; some pins have boot, Flash, or input-only restrictions.
Serial transmit and receive for debugging and communication.
EN resets the chip; BOOT selects firmware download mode.
steps: Connect to a computer over USB and install an ESP32 development environment.
Write a program to control an LED or read a sensor.
Send the collected data over Wi-Fi.

stm32.name: STM32F103C8T6
stm32.subtitle: 32-bit Arm microcontroller
stm32.description: A microcontroller integrating a processor, memory, and multiple peripherals. A program reads inputs, makes decisions, and controls external devices such as lights and motors.
stm32.tip: Fine leads extending from all four sides identify the LQFP package. The dot marks pin 1; confirm that the datasheet drawing is a top view.
pinNotes: Digital power and ground; place decoupling capacitors near every supply pair.
General-purpose I/O; many pins also serve serial, timer, and other peripheral functions.
steps: Provide stable power, decoupling, and boot configuration.
Program the device through SWD using an ST-LINK.
Configure GPIO or a timer to light an LED.

ne555.name: NE555P
ne555.subtitle: Classic timer
ne555.description: Uses resistors and a capacitor to set a delay or generate continuous pulses. It provides an accessible introduction to oscillation, timing, and duty cycle.
ne555.tip: With the notch at the top in a top view, pin 1 is at the upper left and numbering proceeds counterclockwise. A common DIP pitch is 2.54 mm, convenient for breadboards.
pinNotes: Trigger and threshold inputs sense capacitor voltage.
Signal output and capacitor discharge terminal.
steps: Build the astable oscillator from the datasheet.
The capacitor repeatedly charges and discharges, producing high and low output levels.
Change the resistance or capacitance and observe the LED flash period.

lm358.name: LM358D
lm358.subtitle: Dual operational amplifier
lm358.description: Contains two operational amplifiers. Feedback resistors let it amplify small sensor signals or form filters and voltage followers.
lm358.tip: SOIC leads bend outward into a gull-wing profile. Check both the input common-mode range and output swing when designing the circuit.
pinNotes: Inverting and noninverting inputs of amplifier 1.
Noninverting and inverting inputs of amplifier 2.
Negative supply or ground, and positive supply.
steps: Connect the sensor voltage to the noninverting input.
Use resistors to establish negative feedback and set closed-loop gain.
Feed the amplified signal to an ADC.

atmega.name: ATmega328P-PU
atmega.subtitle: 8-bit AVR microcontroller
atmega.description: The main controller used by the classic Arduino Uno. It executes programs, reads analog voltages, generates PWM, and communicates with other chips over serial interfaces.
atmega.tip: The model shows the 28-pin DIP version; other packages are available. Operation at 20 MHz requires a 4.5–5.5 V supply; check the speed grade for other voltages.
pinNotes: Digital and analog power, and common ground.
Three I/O ports; selected pins support ADC, PWM, or communications.
Active-low reset, also used during ISP programming.
steps: Provide power, decoupling, and the required clock circuit.
Program through ISP or download using a bootloader.
Read a button and use PWM to vary LED brightness.

wroom.name: ESP32-WROOM-32E
wroom.subtitle: Wi-Fi / Bluetooth module
wroom.description: Integrates the ESP32 chip, Flash, crystal, and RF circuitry on a small board. A metal shield helps reduce electromagnetic interference, while the PCB antenna transmits and receives radio signals.
wroom.tip: The module provides RF circuitry; a complete development board also requires power, a programming interface, and connectors. Preserve the antenna clearance specified by the official guide.
pinNotes: Chip enable; a low level resets the chip.
General-purpose I/O; check alternate functions and boot restrictions before use.
steps: Provide a stable 3.3 V supply on the carrier board.
Reserve antenna clearance according to the recommended layout.
Connect the programming interface and run a wireless application.

rp2040.name: RP2040
rp2040.subtitle: Dual-core Arm microcontroller
rp2040.description: A dual-core Arm Cortex-M0+ MCU with programmable I/O (PIO). RP2040 uses external Flash to store programs; the Pico board integrates this memory.
rp2040.tip: Rotate the model to inspect its underside pads and center pad. RP2040 programs are usually stored in external Flash.
pinNotes: I/O power and ground. Follow the official hardware guide for power domains and decoupling.
General-purpose I/O supporting several alternate peripheral functions.
Connects external Flash for program storage.
steps: Store the program in external QSPI Flash.
The two processor cores execute tasks after startup.
Use PIO state machines to generate precise interface timing.

am3358.name: AM3358BZCZ60
am3358.subtitle: Arm application processor
am3358.description: An Arm Cortex-A8 application processor with graphics and peripheral interfaces for embedded systems running Linux. BGA describes its solder-ball connections; the system also requires external memory, power, and supporting circuitry.
am3358.tip: This is an application-processor example. Rotate it to inspect the 18 × 18 ball array; use the specific device documentation for wiring and ball assignments.
pinNotes: Loads the bootloader from the selected storage device.
The processor core, I/O, and other domains have separate supply requirements.
BGA drawings commonly use letters and numbers to locate balls; check the drawing orientation.
steps: The power-management IC powers each domain in the required sequence.
The bootloader initializes external DDR and other hardware.
The operating system runs applications and manages network and display peripherals.

7805.name: L7805CV
7805.subtitle: 5 V linear regulator
7805.description: Regulates a DC input with sufficient headroom to 5 V. A linear regulator dissipates the input-to-output voltage drop as heat, so load capability depends on cooling.
7805.tip: The metal tab and mounting hole assist heat dissipation. Power loss is approximately (input voltage − output voltage) × current; assess temperature rise for the load.
pinNotes: The input must provide the headroom required by the datasheet.
Common ground; this model’s metal tab also connects to ground.
steps: Apply the DC input to the regulator.
The internal feedback loop regulates the output to 5 V.
Check headroom and load, then calculate cooling needs.

ams1117.name: AMS1117-3.3
ams1117.subtitle: 3.3 V low-dropout regulator
ams1117.description: Provides a fixed 3.3 V low-dropout linear output. Current, dropout, and output-capacitor requirements depend on the manufacturer; this exhibit uses UMW documentation.
ams1117.tip: Three small leads lie on one side, with a wide metal heat-dissipation tab on the other.
pinNotes: The output and large tab are electrically connected.
Input; required headroom depends on load and dropout specifications.
steps: Use an input capacitor to stabilize the upstream supply.
The chip adjusts its internal pass element to maintain 3.3 V.
Select the output capacitor from the datasheet and provide sufficient heat-spreading copper.

drv8833.name: DRV8833PWPR
drv8833.subtitle: Dual H-bridge motor driver
drv8833.description: Two internal H-bridges reverse winding current to drive two DC motors or one bipolar stepper motor. Sustainable current depends on package, supply, and cooling; peak and continuous ratings describe different conditions.
drv8833.tip: Inspect the thermal pad on the underside. Consider motor supply, current, cooling, and recirculation-current layout together.
pinNotes: Power outputs connected to motor windings.
steps: The MCU supplies direction signals and PWM.
The H-bridges reverse current to change motor direction.
The chip detects faults while the thermal design supports continuous operation.

ch340.name: CH340G
ch340.subtitle: USB-to-UART bridge
ch340.description: Transfers data between USB and a UART serial port. The G-suffix version uses an external clock component; other CH340 suffixes have their own packages and features.
ch340.tip: There are eight surface-mount leads on each side; a CH340G circuit usually has an external crystal nearby.
pinNotes: Follow the selected power-supply arrangement for these connections.
steps: The computer enumerates a serial device over USB.
The chip converts between USB packets and UART bit streams.
The MCU receives commands or outputs logs through UART.

max3232.name: MAX3232IPWR
max3232.subtitle: RS-232 level converter
max3232.description: Converts between logic-level serial signals and RS-232 levels, with two drivers and two receivers. UART describes data timing; RS-232 also specifies electrical signaling, so the levels must match the connected interface.
max3232.tip: UART describes serial data transfer, while RS-232 defines interface electrical characteristics. Check both endpoints’ voltage standards before connecting them.
steps: The controller produces logic-level serial signals.
The charge pump generates positive and negative conversion voltages.
The transceiver communicates with external equipment at RS-232 levels.

w25q.name: W25Q32JVSSIQ
w25q.subtitle: 32 Mbit serial Flash
w25q.description: Stores 32 Mbit through SPI, Dual, or Quad interfaces and retains the data without power. 32 Mbit equals 4 MiB; erase and program operations follow device-specific block and page rules.
w25q.tip: 32 Mbit equals 4 MB. A byte contains eight bits; this model uses the 208 mil wide-body SOP-8 version.
pinNotes: Serial data pins whose functions depend on interface mode.
Flash is programmed by page; updates may require sector erasure first.
steps: The controller sends a read command and address over SPI.
The chip returns data from that address.
Follow the erase-and-program sequence when updating data.

24lc256.name: 24LC256-I/P
24lc256.subtitle: I²C EEPROM
24lc256.description: Stores 256 Kbit over I²C with electrical erase/write and power-off retention. 256 Kbit equals 32 KiB; write endurance and write-cycle time have specified limits.
24lc256.tip: EEPROM suits small amounts of configuration data. Write endurance and cycle time influence software design.
pinNotes: I²C data and clock lines with suitable pull-ups.
Address selection allows multiple devices on one bus.
steps: The controller selects the device address and memory location.
Write the configuration data and wait for the write cycle to finish.
Read the retained data when the device powers up again.

ds3231.name: DS3231SN#
ds3231.subtitle: High-accuracy real-time clock
ds3231.description: Provides date and time over I²C using an integrated temperature-compensated crystal oscillator and supports battery backup. A suitable backup supply keeps time after the main supply is removed.
ds3231.tip: The temperature-compensated crystal is integrated. The package is 300 mil wide, and the backup-battery connection sustains timekeeping.
pinNotes: Read and set the date and time.
Backup supply input for timekeeping after main power is removed.
steps: Set the correct date and time.
The internal compensated crystal maintains time.
The controller reads the clock periodically or responds to an alarm interrupt.

hc595.name: SN74HC595N
hc595.subtitle: 8-bit shift register
hc595.description: Receives serial data one bit per clock, then updates eight parallel outputs through a latch. The shift register holds incoming data while the output latch controls when the whole output group changes.
hc595.tip: Eight through-hole leads run along each side; the top marking includes 74HC595.
pinNotes: Latches shift-register data into the outputs.
Eight parallel outputs; observe their load-current ratings.
steps: The MCU sends eight data bits sequentially.
Each shift-clock edge moves data into the register.
A latch operation updates all eight outputs together.

hc00.name: SN74HC00N
hc00.subtitle: Quad 2-input NAND gate
hc00.description: Contains four independent two-input NAND gates; the output goes low when both inputs are high. Logic gates map input levels to defined outputs, and a truth table lists every input combination.
hc00.tip: Seven through-hole leads run along each side; 74HC00 identifies the logic family and gate function.
pinNotes: NAND result: low only when both inputs are high.
Tie unused CMOS inputs to valid logic levels as directed by the datasheet.
steps: Apply a defined high or low level to each input.
Observe all four input combinations.
Record the outputs to build the NAND truth table.

pc817.name: PC817X2NSZ1B
pc817.subtitle: Optocoupler
pc817.description: An internal infrared LED drives a phototransistor optically to transfer a signal between two circuits. Current transfer ratio (CTR) has grades and test conditions; isolation performance depends on the device and complete board design.
pc817.tip: An optocoupler contains a light emitter and receiver. CTR is output current divided by input current and varies with grade and operating conditions.
pinNotes: Input LED anode and cathode; add a current-limiting resistor.
Design the input and output electrical circuits separately.
steps: Input current lights the internal LED.
The light turns on the output phototransistor.
The output circuit detects the change, transferring an isolated signal.

mpu6050.name: MPU-6050
mpu6050.subtitle: Six-axis inertial sensor
mpu6050.description: Measures three-axis acceleration and three-axis angular rate, providing digital data over I²C. Accelerometer readings include gravity; orientation estimation combines sensor data with algorithms.
mpu6050.tip: Six axes means three acceleration axes and three angular-rate axes. Long-term orientation estimation involves drift correction and sensor fusion.
pinNotes: Interrupts for data-ready and other events.
Device power, logic-level reference, and ground.
steps: The accelerometer measures acceleration components along three axes.
The gyroscope measures angular rate about three axes.
Software calibrates and fuses the readings to estimate motion and orientation.

mcp3008.name: MCP3008-I/P
mcp3008.subtitle: 8-channel analog-to-digital converter
mcp3008.description: Converts eight analog inputs into 10-bit digital results read over SPI. A 10-bit conversion has 1024 codes; the reference voltage and other conditions determine the actual input range.
mcp3008.tip: A 10-bit ADC has 1024 quantization levels. Input range, reference quality, and sample rate all influence the result.
pinNotes: Reference voltage defining the conversion range.
SPI clock, data input, data output, and chip select.
Analog and digital grounds; plan their connection according to the datasheet.
steps: Connect the voltage to the chosen channel.
The controller starts sampling over SPI.
Read the 10-bit result and convert it to voltage using VREF.

uno.name: Arduino Uno R3
uno.subtitle: Classic 8-bit development board
uno.description: Combines an ATmega328P, USB, power circuitry, and accessible female headers into a beginner development platform. Its 14 digital I/O and six analog inputs describe the board-level interfaces.
uno.tip: The illustration highlights the socketed DIP controller, USB Type-B port, and expansion headers. Follow the Uno R3 pinout for actual wiring.
pinNotes: Digital I/O; selected pins support PWM.
Analog inputs that can also serve as digital I/O.
Power outputs and ground; observe each rail’s current limit.
Program download, serial communication, and direct programming interfaces.
steps: Connect over USB and select the Uno board.
Write the setup and loop functions.
Upload, connect a button or LED, and observe the inputs and outputs.

pico.name: Raspberry Pi Pico
pico.subtitle: RP2040 development board
pico.description: Integrates RP2040, external Flash, power circuitry, and USB for C/C++ and MicroPython projects. The 40-position main interface includes 26 multifunction GPIO plus power, ground, and other pins.
pico.tip: Castellated board edges allow direct soldering to a carrier, and pin headers can also be fitted. The controller and external Flash are separate devices.
pinNotes: Exposed GPIO numbering has reserved gaps; consult the pinout.
System power, USB power, and regulated 3.3 V output.
Hold while connecting USB to enter firmware download mode.
steps: Hold BOOTSEL while connecting USB.
Copy a UF2 firmware file to the storage device that appears.
Run a MicroPython or C/C++ program to control peripherals.

gy521.name: GY-521 module
gy521.subtitle: MPU-6050 sensor breakout board
gy521.description: Places an MPU-6050 and supporting power circuitry on a small board with accessible connections. Commercial GY-521 versions vary; confirm supply and logic levels against the actual board and its documentation.
gy521.tip: GY-521 boards have multiple manufacturing versions, and this model illustrates a generic form. The documentation link gives functional reference for a similar MPU-6050 module.
pinNotes: Module power and ground; the input range depends on the board’s power design.
steps: Identify the MPU-6050 and surrounding components.
Check the module’s logic levels and connect to a controller over I²C.
Read and calibrate acceleration and angular rate.

nrf24.name: nRF24L01+ module
nrf24.subtitle: 2.4 GHz wireless transceiver module
nrf24.description: Receives host data through SPI and communicates with a peer over 2.4 GHz radio. Both ends require compatible protocols and settings; supply quality and antenna layout affect link performance.
nrf24.tip: The meandering copper trace at the board end is the antenna. Both ends need matching channels, addresses, and data rates to establish a link.
pinNotes: Stable power and ground; decoupling supports transmit-current changes.
Controls operating states such as receive and transmit.
Interrupts for events such as completed data reception.
steps: Set the channel, address, and data rate through SPI.
Load data into the transmit buffer.
The peer module receives the data and passes it to its controller.

tps61040.name: TPS61040DBVR
tps61040.subtitle: Boost DC/DC converter
tps61040.description: Uses switching action, an inductor, and a diode to raise a DC input voltage. Feedback resistors set the output voltage, commonly for low-power bias supplies.
tps61040.tip: A five-pin SOT-23 has three leads on one side and two on the other. The inductor, diode, and capacitors are essential parts of the boost circuit.
pinNotes: Switch node connected to the inductor and rectifier diode.
Feedback input; a resistor divider sets the target voltage.
steps: The inductor stores energy while the switch conducts.
When the switch opens, the inductor transfers energy to the output through the diode.
Feedback adjusts switching to maintain the target voltage.

1n4148.name: 1N4148
1n4148.subtitle: Glass-packaged fast switching diode
1n4148.description: A small-signal diode for steering, clamping, and fast switching. The black band on its glass body marks cathode K; the electrical data here reference the Vishay 1N4148.
1n4148.tip: Maximum ratings require the associated temperature and power conditions. Start learning experiments at low voltage and current, and check the purchased manufacturer’s datasheet.
pinNotes: The black-banded end. The bar in the circuit symbol also indicates the cathode.
The opposite end of the glass body; conventional forward current flows from A to K.
Trimmed lead lengths and mounting orientation vary; cross-check the band using a multimeter’s diode mode.
steps: Locate the black cathode band and match it to K in the schematic.
With power disconnected, measure both directions in diode mode; forward conduction usually displays a voltage drop.
Choose connections for the required current, reverse voltage, and dissipation.

1n4007.name: 1N4007
1n4007.subtitle: Axial general-purpose rectifier diode
1n4007.description: A black cylindrical body with axial leads, commonly used for power rectification and slow flyback paths. The band marks cathode K; the electrical data here reference the Vishay 1N4007.
1n4007.tip: The 1 A rating includes a 9.5 mm lead-length condition; calculate temperature rise in the actual design. Check reverse-recovery performance for high-frequency switching-supply rectification.
pinNotes: The banded end, corresponding to the bar in the circuit symbol.
The opposite end; conventional forward current flows from A to K.
For a DC coil, K usually connects to the positive coil supply and A to the switched end.
steps: Read the body marking and locate the cathode band.
Confirm the forward direction using a multimeter’s diode mode.
Wire the low-voltage experiment and check current and heating.

ss14.name: SS14
ss14.subtitle: Surface-mount Schottky rectifier
ss14.description: A Schottky structure provides a low forward drop, useful in low-voltage supplies. The SMA body has solder terminals at each end and a cathode band; data reference the Vishay SS14.
specs: 1 A, with datasheet temperature and pad conditions
ss14.tip: Schottky reverse leakage changes significantly with temperature; check reverse voltage, conduction loss, and PCB heat-spreading copper.
pinNotes: The body band marks K; verify pad orientation from the manufacturer’s package drawing.
The other terminal is A; forward current flows from A to K.
Top codes and band styles vary by manufacturer; use the purchased part number and package drawing together.
steps: Confirm the purchased part number is SS14 and locate the cathode band.
Align the component band with the PCB’s K mark.
After soldering, inspect orientation, joints, and shorts with power disconnected.

2n3904.name: 2N3904
2n3904.subtitle: NPN small-signal transistor
2n3904.description: Base current controls collector current for small-signal amplification and low-power switching. The TO-92 body has one flat face; this entry uses the onsemi 2N3904 pin assignment.
2n3904.tip: Add a base current-limiting resistor. Size base drive using saturation specifications while observing collector-current and dissipation limits; provide flyback protection for inductive loads.
pinNotes: For this reference part, with the flat face toward you and leads down, the left lead is pin 1, E.
The center lead is B, driven through a resistor.
The right lead is pin 3, C, commonly connected to the controlled load.
TO-92 devices use several pin arrangements; verify E, B, and C individually when substituting parts.
steps: Face the flat side forward with leads down and identify E, B, and C from the datasheet.
Calculate base and load current-limiting resistors for the LED or small load.
Use a low-voltage current-limited supply and observe switching and temperature rise.

irlz44n.name: IRLZ44N
irlz44n.subtitle: Logic-level N-channel power MOSFET
irlz44n.description: Gate-source voltage controls drain-source conduction, commonly for DC motor and LED-strip switching. The metal mounting tab is electrically connected to the drain; data reference the Infineon IRLZ44NPbF.
irlz44n.tip: The 47 A rating depends on case temperature and cooling. Gate threshold describes the onset of tiny current; calculate load capability from on-resistance at the actual VGS and resulting temperature rise.
pinNotes: With the marked face forward and leads down, the left lead G takes the drive signal; a series gate resistor and pull-down are common.
The center lead D connects to the switched load; the rear metal tab also connects to D.
The right lead S is grounded in a typical low-side circuit; drive voltage is referenced to S.
For 3.3 V control, verify conduction performance at that voltage and establish a clear common reference for gate and driver.
steps: Identify G, D, and S and check the tab’s electrical connection.
Choose drive voltage, cooling, and inductive-load protection for the load current.
Use a current-limited supply and a small initial load to check on-state voltage drop and temperature rise.

led-red-5mm.name: 5 mm red LED
led-red-5mm.subtitle: Two-lead through-hole LED
led-red-5mm.description: Emits red light when forward current flows, making it useful for circuit-state indication. The model shows a common 5 mm two-lead structure; the voltage example uses the Kingbright WP7113ID.
specs: Select for the specific part and temperature; add series current limiting
led-red-5mm.tip: Choose a target current, then calculate the series resistor as R ≈ (supply voltage − LED forward voltage) / current; check resistor power and GPIO current capability.
pinNotes: On a common new component, the longer lead is A and connects toward the higher-potential current-limited branch.
The shorter lead and flattened rim commonly mark K; confirm with the specific package drawing.
Use body polarity marks, the manufacturer’s drawing, and a diode-mode test.
steps: Identify anode A and cathode K.
Calculate and insert a series resistor before connecting a low-voltage DC supply.
Measure current, observe brightness, and check rated conditions.

rgb-led-5mm.name: 5 mm common-cathode RGB LED
rgb-led-5mm.subtitle: Three LED dies sharing one cathode
rgb-led-5mm.description: Red, green, and blue LED dies share one body and mix colors through three controlled currents. The model illustrates the common-cathode structure of the Kingbright WP154A4SUREQBFZGC.
specs: One resistor for each red, green, and blue channel
rgb-led-5mm.tip: Check forward voltage and efficiency separately for each color. Common-cathode and common-anode parts look similar; confirm the common-terminal type before designing the driver, and verify the part-specific color pin order.
pinNotes: Reference-part pin 2 is K and the longer lead; all three colors share it.
Reference-part pin 1 is the red anode, connected to its own current-limiting branch.
Reference-part pin 3 is blue and pin 4 is green, each with a separate resistor.
Read pin numbers from the manufacturer’s specified view; retain the assigned numbers when rotating the model.
steps: Use the manufacturer’s drawing to identify the common cathode and color leads.
Add a separate resistor for each color and light them individually at low current.
Adjust brightness with three PWM channels and observe color mixing.

tactile-6x6.name: 6 × 6 mm tactile switch
tactile-6x6.subtitle: Four-lead normally-open momentary switch
tactile-6x6.description: Pressing connects two contact groups, and releasing returns the mechanism. The four leads form two internally connected pairs; this generic structure can be compared with the Omron B3F family.
specs: Check the complete part number and load type in the datasheet
tactile-6x6.tip: With power disconnected, use continuity mode to identify the two internally connected pairs. Add a pull-up or pull-down for the input and handle mechanical contact bounce.
pinNotes: These leads remain connected in both released and pressed states; group names are teaching labels.
The other internally connected pair forms the second node.
Pressing joins the groups; releasing separates them. Determine physical pair positions from the datasheet and continuity measurements.
steps: With power disconnected, identify the two always-connected lead pairs.
Choose one lead from each pair for the input circuit.
Check logic levels when pressed and released, then add debouncing.

spdt-slide.name: Three-terminal slide switch
spdt-slide.subtitle: SPDT, two maintained positions
spdt-slide.description: The slider moves between two positions, connecting the common contact COM to one of two selectable terminals. The model shows a three-terminal SPDT ON-ON structure, with the circuit form referenced to the C&K JS series.
specs: Check the exact part and DC load in the datasheet
spdt-slide.tip: The middle terminal is commonly COM on three-terminal versions; confirm the actual part with a continuity test. Determine the connection corresponding to each slider direction from its internal structure and manufacturer drawing.
pinNotes: Connects to one of the two selectable terminals in each position; commonly the middle terminal.
Connected to COM in the first position.
Connected to COM in the second position; identify metal mounting tabs separately using the mechanical drawing.
steps: Measure continuity between the three terminals in both positions.
Identify COM and record the selected terminal for each position.
Check contact ratings before connecting a mode-selection or low-voltage switching circuit.

usb-c-24.name: USB-C 24-contact receptacle
usb-c-24.subtitle: Reversible power and data interface
usb-c-24.description: An insulating tongue sits inside a metal shield, with the full interface arranging 24 contacts on its two sides. The model illustrates the connector family and can be compared with GCT USB4080; PCB solder-tail arrangements vary by exact model.
specs: Determined jointly by connector, cable and circuitry
Determined by the exact connector and system negotiation conditions
usb-c-24.tip: Check mechanical footprint, CC circuitry and target protocol together. Products with the same connector outline may use different solder-tail counts and data-channel arrangements.
pinNotes: Power and ground each have several contacts; assess routing and current capacity for the complete design.
Identify plug orientation and connection state, and participate in power-capability detection or USB PD communication.
Connect USB 2.0 and high-speed differential signals in their groups; the system design determines which channels are used.
SBU supports the applicable modes; treat shield solder tabs according to the grounding plan.
steps: Confirm the purchased receptacle’s 24-contact arrangement and PCB footprint drawing.
Check power, CC, data and shield connections for the required protocol.
Inspect for shorts after soldering, then verify both orientations and power behavior according to the design.

jst-xh-2.name: JST XH two-pin connector
jst-xh-2.subtitle: 2.50 mm-pitch wire-to-board connection
jst-xh-2.description: The shrouded board header mates with a crimp-contact cable housing, commonly for power or simple signals. The model illustrates the two-position vertical board header of the XH family.
jst-xh-2.tip: Assess current capacity using the contacts, wire size, crimp quality and temperature rise together; select mutually compatible XH housings, contacts and board headers.
pinNotes: Its signal function is defined by the board; consult the PCB markings and schematic.
Also assigned by the circuit; trace power polarity through every harness endpoint.
Shrouds and latches define insertion direction; the designer assigns the circuit’s positive and negative positions.
steps: Check the series, 2.50 mm pitch, position count and mating part numbers.
Confirm the electrical function and polarity of both wires from board markings.
Make suitable crimps, mate the connector, and check terminal locking and retention with a gentle pull.

header-2x5.name: 2 × 5 dual-row pin header
header-2x5.subtitle: 2.54 mm pitch, ten through-hole pins
header-2x5.description: Ten metal pins are arranged in two rows of five and retained by an insulating plastic strip. The model uses a generic vertical header structure, comparable to the Samtec TSW-105 dual-row configuration.
specs: Determined by pin material, plating, mating half and complete part number
header-2x5.tip: Find the PCB pin-1 mark and read the interface definition; several debugging protocols use similar headers. Check orientation and the position of every row when mating.
pinNotes: Usually identified by a square PCB pad, the number 1 or a triangle; the design documentation is authoritative.
Dual-row interfaces commonly put odd and even numbers in separate rows; some designs number by row. Follow the schematic.
Each pin conducts independently; the application circuit assigns GND, power and signal functions.
steps: Confirm 2 × 5 positions and 2.54 mm pitch.
Locate pin 1 and check every item in the interface table.
Align all ten pins when mating, and inspect for a one-column offset or reversed connection.

screw-terminal-2.name: Two-position screw terminal block
screw-terminal-2.subtitle: 5.08 mm pitch, PCB-mounted wire clamp
screw-terminal-2.description: A screw-driven clamp secures an external wire to a PCB contact. The model represents the two-position 5.08 mm PCB terminal family, comparable to Phoenix Contact MKDS 1,5/2-5,08.
specs: Check the complete part number and applicable standards
screw-terminal-2.tip: Select wire size, stripping length and tightening torque according to the manufacturer. Secure the wire after inserting it into the clamping opening, then gently pull to check retention.
pinNotes: One wire-clamping opening and its corresponding PCB pin form a single contact.
A second independent contact; its electrical function follows the PCB marking and schematic.
Screws provide mechanical clamping; the circuit defines polarity. Trace wire destinations before connecting.
steps: Disconnect power and verify both terminals’ electrical functions.
Strip the wire as specified and insert the conductor fully into the clamping area.
Tighten to the specified torque, gently check retention, and confirm spacing between adjacent terminals.

resistor-1k.name: 1 kΩ axial resistor
resistor-1k.subtitle: Limit current and divide voltage with resistance
resistor-1k.description: Metal leads extend from both ends of a cylindrical resistor body, with colored bands encoding resistance and tolerance. The model uses a four-band 1 kΩ, ±5% teaching example; actual power rating and dimensions depend on the product.
specs: Determined by complete part number and temperature-derating curve
resistor-1k.tip: Use I = V/R and P = I²R to calculate current and dissipation. The bands encode resistance and tolerance; obtain rated power from the model documentation.
pinNotes: An ordinary fixed resistor is nonpolarized; its ends are interchangeable in DC wiring.
Brown is 1, black is 0 and red is ×100, giving 1000 Ω.
Gold indicates ±5%; first identify the tolerance band, which is spaced from the others.
steps: Read from the value bands toward the tolerance band and confirm brown, black, red, gold.
Measure resistance with power off; consider parallel paths when measuring in circuit.
Calculate expected dissipation and select a power rating with margin.

ceramic-100nf.name: 100 nF ceramic-disc capacitor
ceramic-100nf.subtitle: Disc-shaped, two-lead nonpolarized capacitor
ceramic-100nf.description: A ceramic dielectric and two electrodes form a capacitor, often enclosed in a coated disc. The model illustrates a 100 nF ceramic-disc capacitor family; verify dimensions, voltage rating, tolerance and dielectric class for the purchased part.
specs: Check the complete marking and manufacturer datasheet
ceramic-100nf.tip: 104 encodes capacitance; read the complete marking or datasheet for voltage rating. Shorten leads and loops for bypassing, and check the frequency behavior required by the circuit.
pinNotes: The two leads connect to internal electrodes; ordinary ceramic-disc capacitor terminals are interchangeable.
In pF, the first two digits are significant figures and the third is the power of ten.
Other components also use disc shapes; identify the part using its capacitance code, part number and circuit location.
steps: Read the 104 capacitance code and check the complete part number and rated voltage.
Choose placement according to bypass, filtering or coupling use.
Install with power off and the capacitor discharged; keep bypass leads and loops short.

electrolytic-100uf.name: 100 µF aluminum electrolytic capacitor
electrolytic-100uf.subtitle: Polarized, radial two-lead energy-storage capacitor
electrolytic-100uf.description: The cylindrical aluminum can contains electrodes and electrolyte, suitable for power filtering and energy storage. The model represents an ordinary polarized radial aluminum electrolytic capacitor; parts with the same capacitance have various voltage, size and ripple ratings.
specs: Confirm from the complete body marking and datasheet
Check the series, capacitance and case dimensions
electrolytic-100uf.tip: Keep operating voltage, including ripple peaks, within the rating, and assess ripple current and temperature. Before handling, discharge through a suitable resistor and measure terminal voltage.
pinNotes: Ordinary radial aluminum electrolytics commonly mark negative with a side stripe containing minus signs; confirm the manufacturer’s marking.
The positive lead is commonly longer on new parts; combine lead length with body markings after cutting or forming.
Some sizes have scored pressure-release vents on top. Leave the required clearance, and use the leads for circuit connections.
steps: Check 100 µF, rated voltage and the side negative stripe.
Verify polarity and operating voltage, including ripple peaks, against the schematic.
Switch off, discharge and measure terminal voltage before fitting, then perform a low-voltage power-on check.

hc04.name: SN74HC04N
hc04.subtitle: Hex inverter
hc04.description: Six independent inverters change high logic levels to low and low levels to high. The device changes control-signal polarity and supports learning the most basic logic operation.
hc04.tip: The top notch establishes orientation. Connect pin 14 to VCC and pin 7 to GND. Tie unused CMOS inputs to valid logic levels.
pinNotes: The inverted output corresponding to each input.
Power and ground; place a decoupling capacitor nearby.
steps: Apply a high or low level to one A input.
Observe the opposite level at its Y output.
Test each channel and draw the inverter truth table.

hc14.name: SN74HC14N
hc14.subtitle: Hex Schmitt-trigger inverter
hc14.description: All six inverters have Schmitt-trigger inputs. Separate rising and falling switching thresholds turn slowly changing signals into clean digital edges.
hc14.tip: Hysteresis is the gap between rising and falling switching thresholds. An RC network and Schmitt-trigger input can implement switch debouncing.
pinNotes: Input with hysteresis; its voltage must remain within the allowed range.
steps: Use a resistor and capacitor to generate a slowly changing input.
Observe output transitions when the input crosses a threshold.
Compare switching points during rising and falling transitions.

hc08.name: SN74HC08N
hc08.subtitle: Quad two-input AND gate
hc08.description: Four two-input AND gates produce a high output only when both inputs are high. They express control relationships requiring several conditions to be true together.
hc08.tip: Treat the two inputs as two switch conditions; the output indicates whether both are true. LED experiments require series current-limiting resistors.
pinNotes: The two logic inputs of each AND gate.
High when both A and B are high.
steps: Connect switchable logic levels to A and B.
Test 00, 01, 10 and 11 in sequence.
Record Y and observe the case in which both conditions are true.

hc32.name: SN74HC32N
hc32.subtitle: Quad two-input OR gate
hc32.description: Four two-input OR gates produce a high output when either input is high. They commonly combine several trigger conditions.
hc32.tip: An OR gate actively generates its output level. Feed multiple push-pull signals into separate OR-gate inputs to combine them.
pinNotes: The two inputs of each OR gate.
High when at least one input is high.
steps: Set the two inputs individually high or low.
Observe the output when either condition is true.
Write the truth table for all four input combinations.

hc86.name: SN74HC86N
hc86.subtitle: Quad two-input XOR gate
hc86.description: Four independent XOR gates each compare two inputs. Different levels produce high; matching levels produce low. XOR supports binary addition and parity checking.
hc86.tip: The common XOR symbol is ⊕. A half adder uses XOR for the sum bit and AND for the carry bit.
pinNotes: The two inputs to the XOR operation.
steps: Enumerate the four input combinations.
Compare Y with the least significant bit of binary addition.
Add an AND gate to observe sum and carry.

hc74.name: SN74HC74N
hc74.subtitle: Dual D-type flip-flop
hc74.description: Two flip-flops each store one bit of state. They sample D on the clock’s rising edge and retain the result at Q, supporting frequency division, state storage and synchronization.
hc74.tip: Data must meet setup and hold times around the clock edge. PRE# and CLR# are active-low asynchronous controls.
pinNotes: Stored state and its complementary output.
Asynchronous set and clear; use combinations according to the function table.
steps: Set D and keep asynchronous controls inactive.
Apply a rising edge to CLK that meets timing requirements.
Observe Q retaining the sampled data.

hc138.name: SN74HC138N
hc138.subtitle: 3-to-8 line decoder
hc138.description: A three-bit binary address becomes one of eight selection signals. When enabled, the addressed output goes low, allowing selection of memory or other peripherals.
hc138.tip: An overbar or # indicates active low. Confirm enable conditions, then select an output using the C, B and A combination.
pinNotes: Three address bits; A is the least significant bit.
One active-high and two active-low enables.
steps: Set all three enables to their active combination.
Apply addresses 0 through 7.
Observe the active-low selection moving between outputs.

cd4017.name: CD4017BE
cd4017.subtitle: Decade counter and decoder
cd4017.description: Each valid clock moves the high level to the next of ten decoded outputs. Combining counting and decoding makes this device useful for running-light and sequencing demonstrations.
cd4017.tip: Output numbers and physical pin numbers have separate meanings. Locate Q0–Q9 using the datasheet and check drive current before connecting LEDs.
pinNotes: A rising edge advances the count while clock inhibit is low.
Ten decoded outputs that go high in sequence during normal counting.
High levels reset the count or pause clock counting.
Power, ground and carry output for division or cascading.
steps: Reset the counter so Q0 is the initial state.
Apply slow clock pulses.
Observe the ten outputs cycling in sequence.

cd4066.name: CD4066BE
cd4066.subtitle: Quad bilateral analog switch
cd4066.description: Four independent electronic switches are each controlled by a digital level. When closed, each path carries analog or digital signals in either direction within the allowed range.
cd4066.tip: A closed switch has on-resistance that varies with supply and signal voltage. Keep signal voltages within the device’s allowed supply range.
pinNotes: The pair of input/output terminals on each switch carries signals in either direction.
Independent control for each channel; high closes the switch.
Upper and lower supply rails determine the available signal range.
steps: Place one switch in series with a low-voltage signal path.
Change the corresponding control logic level.
Measure the open/closed state and signal changes while conducting.

cd4051.name: CD4051BE
cd4051.subtitle: 8-to-1 analog multiplexer
cd4051.description: A three-bit address selects one of eight channels to connect to the common terminal. The bidirectional path lets several slow analog signals take turns feeding one ADC.
cd4051.tip: Allow settling time after switching before sampling. On-resistance, load and ADC input capacitance jointly affect the reading.
pinNotes: Eight channels and the common signal terminal.
Positive supply, logic ground and analog negative-supply reference.
steps: Connect signals to the channels and the common terminal to the sampling input.
Set the address to select a signal.
Wait for settling, sample, and move to the next channel.

lvc245.name: SN74LVC245APWR
lvc245.subtitle: Octal bus transceiver
lvc245.description: Signals pass between two eight-bit data buses, with one control selecting the direction for the whole group. Three-state outputs release the bus for buffering and shared-bus interfaces.
lvc245.tip: VCC determines the output-high level. DIR controls the group direction and OE# controls bus drive; check logic thresholds at both ends.
pinNotes: Two banks of eight data terminals.
Selects transfer from A to B or B to A.
Low enables outputs; high selects high impedance.
steps: Set the supply and verify both sides’ logic-level requirements.
Set DIR, then drive OE# low.
Observe eight-bit transfer and high-impedance bus release.

at24c02.name: AT24C02C-PUM
at24c02.subtitle: 2 Kbit I²C EEPROM
at24c02.description: A serial memory stores small amounts of configuration data and retains them after power is removed. I²C accesses 256 bytes for addresses, settings or calibration values.
at24c02.tip: Page writes have boundaries and require an internal write-cycle wait. Handle acknowledge polling and memory endurance according to the datasheet.
pinNotes: I²C data and clock, requiring pull-up resistors.
Select the bus address for multiple devices on shared lines.
steps: Select the device address and target byte position.
Write data and wait for the internal write cycle to finish.
Cycle power, then read and verify the contents.

mb85rc256.name: MB85RC256V
mb85rc256.subtitle: 256 Kbit ferroelectric RAM
mb85rc256.description: Ferroelectric cells support frequent reads and writes while retaining data through power loss. The host accesses 32 KiB through I²C to save operating counts and frequently changing state.
mb85rc256.tip: FRAM completes writes within bus timing. Retention time depends on temperature, and the system power-down process must still preserve a complete record.
steps: Specify the memory address over I²C.
Write the latest count or state.
Read the record at the next startup to restore operation.

w5500.name: W5500
w5500.subtitle: Hardware TCP/IP Ethernet controller
w5500.description: TCP/IP processing, Ethernet MAC and PHY are integrated in one chip. A microcontroller accesses socket buffers over SPI; network magnetics and a jack complete a wired-network device.
w5500.tip: Twelve leads on each of four sides form LQFP-48. Follow official schematics for jack and transformer connections, differential routing and supply decoupling.
pinNotes: Differential transmit/receive terminals connected to network magnetics.
Configure power domains and external clock connections according to the reference design.
steps: Configure the MAC address and network settings through SPI.
Establish a TCP or UDP socket.
Read and write buffers to exchange data over Ethernet.

mcp2515.name: MCP2515-I/P
mcp2515.subtitle: Stand-alone CAN protocol controller
mcp2515.description: The chip receives host commands over SPI and handles CAN frame formatting, filtering and transmit/receive buffers. With an external CAN transceiver, it connects a general microcontroller to a classic CAN network.
mcp2515.tip: MCP2515 handles the protocol; transceivers such as TJA1050 handle bus electrical signaling. Configure CAN bit timing using the crystal frequency and target bit rate.
pinNotes: Logic signals connected to the CAN transceiver.
steps: Configure the CAN bit rate and receive filters from the host.
Write a message into the transmit buffer.
The controller generates a CAN frame that the transceiver sends onto the bus.

tja1050.name: TJA1050T
tja1050.subtitle: High-speed CAN transceiver
tja1050.description: The device converts a CAN controller’s logic into differential levels on CANH and CANL, then restores received signals for the controller. It provides the electrical connection between a node and the CAN bus.
tja1050.tip: Place termination resistors at the two CAN-network ends according to bus requirements. When connecting a 3.3 V MCU, check transmit-input and receive-output levels individually.
pinNotes: Transmit input and receive output connected to the CAN controller.
steps: The CAN controller outputs a sequence of logic bits.
The transceiver converts them into differential-bus states.
The receiving transceiver restores logic levels for CAN-controller decoding.

max485.name: MAX485CPA+
max485.subtitle: Half-duplex RS-485 transceiver
max485.description: The device translates between a logic-level interface such as UART and an RS-485 differential bus. Transmit and receive share one wire pair; enable signals switch direction for multi-node wired communication.
max485.tip: Coordinate bus transmitters so they take turns. Design termination, biasing and a common reference for the bus topology.
pinNotes: Logic transmit input and receive output.
Transmit enable and active-low receive enable.
Differential-bus terminals; verify the definitions at both ends.
steps: The host enables transmission and outputs serial data.
Data travels as the differential voltage between A and B.
Release the transmitter and switch to receiving the reply.

cp2102n.name: CP2102N-A02-GQFN28
cp2102n.subtitle: USB-to-UART bridge with integrated clock
cp2102n.description: The chip converts USB data into UART serial data and integrates a USB transceiver and clock. A computer driver exposes a virtual serial port for exchanging commands and logs with a microcontroller.
cp2102n.tip: CP2102N has 20-, 24- and 28-pin versions. Supply and I/O assignments vary by version; this model represents GQFN28.
pinNotes: UART transmit and receive; connect each to the other device’s corresponding receive or transmit.
Internal-regulator input, device supply and ground; connect according to the supply scheme.
steps: Connect USB to the computer so the driver creates a serial-port interface.
Set the baud rate and data format to match the target.
Transfer programming data or debug logs through UART.

pcf8574.name: PCF8574P
pcf8574.subtitle: Eight-bit I²C I/O expander
pcf8574.description: The I²C bus expands to eight quasi-bidirectional I/O pins for switches or indicators. An interrupt output can prompt the host to read the port when input states change.
pcf8574.tip: Write 1 to a port bit before using it as an input. Check the quasi-bidirectional port’s pull-high and pull-low drive characteristics separately.
pinNotes: Address selection and open-drain interrupt output.
steps: Set the I²C address using the address pins.
Write the port state or set target bits for input use.
Read switch states or update indicators.

ds18b20.name: DS18B20+
ds18b20.subtitle: 1-Wire digital temperature sensor
ds18b20.description: One data line returns digital temperature, and each chip has a unique 64-bit identification code. A host can place several sensors on the same bus and individually request conversions and readings.
ds18b20.tip: TO-92 can contain a complete digital sensor. Match the datasheet’s viewing direction when wiring. DQ requires a pull-up, and parasite power also requires the specified strong-pull-up conditions.
pinNotes: External supply; follow the datasheet for parasite-power wiring.
steps: Identify sensor addresses on the bus.
Issue a temperature-conversion command and wait for completion.
Read temperature and check data, then convert to degrees Celsius.

lm75b.name: LM75BD
lm75b.subtitle: I²C temperature sensor with overtemperature alarm
lm75b.description: The device continuously converts its die temperature into digital readings for the host over I²C. Programmable thresholds and hysteresis operate the OS output to alert the system to excessive temperature.
lm75b.tip: 0.125 °C is the readout step size; accuracy follows the error specification. Sensor location and nearby heat sources affect the measured temperature.
pinNotes: Open-drain overtemperature output, configurable for comparator or interrupt mode.
steps: Set temperature thresholds and hysteresis from the host.
Read the temperature register periodically.
Control fans and alarms using OS or the readings.

pic16f877a.name: PIC16F877A-I/P
pic16f877a.subtitle: Classic 8-bit PIC microcontroller
pic16f877a.description: An 8-bit MCU integrates Flash, ADC, timers and serial interfaces. The 40-pin through-hole package makes power, ports, clocks and programming-signal roles easy to observe.
pic16f877a.tip: PIC program memory is often expressed in instruction words; each program word here is 14 bits. Configure port analog and digital functions before applying analog signals.
pinNotes: Several I/O ports; some pins multiplex ADC and communication peripherals.
Connect every power and ground pin according to the datasheet.
steps: Prepare clock, power, reset and ICSP connections.
Program Flash with a compatible programmer.
Read the ADC, then control outputs using a timer or GPIO.

at89s52.name: AT89S52-24PU
at89s52.subtitle: Classic 8051-architecture microcontroller
at89s52.description: Compatible with the 8051 instruction set, it integrates program Flash, four ports, timers and a serial interface. It is a classic teaching device for registers, peripherals and interrupts.
at89s52.tip: Configure pull-ups for P0’s open-drain behavior when using general-purpose I/O. RST is active high, and EA connects to a valid high level when using internal program memory.
pinNotes: Four eight-bit ports, with some pins also serving communication or bus functions.
ISP programming interface multiplexed on P1.
steps: Configure power, crystal, reset and EA.
Program a blinking-light application through ISP.
Use timer interrupts to control the LED rhythm.

stm32f407.name: STM32F407VGT6
stm32f407.subtitle: Cortex-M4 MCU with floating-point unit
stm32f407.description: The Cortex-M4 core includes DSP instructions and a single-precision floating-point unit for real-time signal processing. Extensive timing, sampling and communication peripherals support more complex control systems.
stm32f407.tip: The 100-pin package has 25 pins per side. Check the complete memory, package and temperature suffixes; power domains also include analog supply and core-regulator support terminals.
pinNotes: Digital and analog supplies, with separate decoupling.
Configure ADC, timer or communication functions on the selected physical pins.
Reset, boot mode and external capacitors for the internal regulator.
steps: Initialize clocks, power and required peripherals.
Download the program through SWD.
Move sampled data using DMA, then perform real-time processing.

stm32g030.name: STM32G030F6P6
stm32g030.subtitle: Compact Cortex-M0+ MCU
stm32g030.description: A 20-pin surface-mount package integrates a 32-bit core, Flash, ADC and timers. It can handle power management, switch inputs and small-device control with a limited pin count.
stm32g030.tip: TSSOP-20 peripheral availability depends on actual pin multiplexing. Start with the internal clock and retain the SWD debug interface.
pinNotes: General-purpose I/O and alternate functions; select them using the TSSOP-20 pin diagram.
External reset input; its function depends on configuration.
steps: Build a minimal system using the internal clock.
Program through SWD and configure GPIO.
Read the ADC or generate PWM to implement a control function.

ch32v003.name: CH32V003F4P6
ch32v003.subtitle: Small RISC-V microcontroller
ch32v003.description: A WCH QingKe RISC-V core is combined with an ADC, timers and common serial interfaces. Small memories and a compact package suit learning concise embedded-control programs.
ch32v003.tip: This series uses a single-wire SDI debug interface. Confirm debug mode and target power before connecting tools such as WCH-Link.
pinNotes: General-purpose I/O and peripheral alternate functions.
Multiplexed pin for the single-wire debug interface.
Reset-function pin; the precise alternate function depends on configuration.
steps: Connect power and single-wire debugging.
Compile and download a RISC-V program.
Use timers, GPIO or ADC for a control experiment.

esp8266ex.name: ESP8266EX
esp8266ex.subtitle: Wi-Fi wireless microcontroller
esp8266ex.description: Integrates a 32-bit processor and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi in one chip. With external flash, a clock, and supporting RF circuitry, it can run programs and connect to wireless networks.
esp8266ex.tip: A bare-chip design needs external storage, RF matching, and an antenna. Set the boot states of GPIO0, GPIO2, and GPIO15 according to the datasheet.
pinNotes: Decouple digital and RF supplies according to the reference design.
External flash interface and RF antenna connection.
steps: Load the application from external flash.
Configure Wi-Fi and join an access point.
Read sensors and send their data over the network.

esp32s3.name: ESP32-S3
esp32s3.subtitle: Dual-core Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE MCU
esp32s3.description: Dual Xtensa LX7 cores integrate Wi-Fi, Bluetooth LE, and extensive peripherals. Camera, display, and USB connections support connected interfaces and edge signal processing.
esp32s3.tip: This exhibit represents the base ESP32-S3 chip, whose program flash is provided externally. Other suffix variants can integrate flash or PSRAM within the package.
pinNotes: Digital and analog supplies and ground, connected by power domain.
Can be multiplexed as USB D− and D+.
Memory interface and RF antenna terminal.
steps: Configure external flash, power, and boot circuitry.
Write the application through a supported programming interface.
Schedule both cores and peripherals for connected acquisition and interaction.

attiny85.name: ATtiny85-20PU
attiny85.subtitle: Eight-pin AVR microcontroller
attiny85.description: An eight-pin package integrates an 8-bit processor, program memory, an ADC, and timers. It supports lighting, buttons, and simple sensor control within a small pin and memory budget.
attiny85.tip: 20 MHz operation requires a 4.5–5.5 V supply. PB5 normally serves as RESET, so the usable I/O count depends on fuse settings and the programming method.
pinNotes: Port pins with multiplexed ADC, timer, and other functions.
Reset and serial programming share some port pins.
Optional clock and universal serial interface functions share I/O.
steps: Apply power and retain the ISP programming connections.
Write the program and select a suitable clock configuration.
Program the device to control LEDs or read buttons and analog inputs.

tl072.name: TL072CP
tl072.subtitle: Dual operational amplifier
tl072.description: Contains two operational amplifiers. It amplifies weak analog signals and can form audio filters with external resistors and capacitors.
tl072.tip: Allow supply-rail headroom for both input voltage range and output swing. Check the complete part number to distinguish TL072 from later H-series versions.
pinNotes: Noninverting and inverting inputs for each channel.
Positive and negative supply terminals. Total supply is their voltage difference.
steps: The input receives the analog signal to be processed.
The external feedback network sets gain or filtering.
The output varies continuously with the input to form the processed signal.

lm324.name: LM324N
lm324.subtitle: Quad operational amplifier
lm324.description: Packs four operational amplifiers into one through-hole package. It can process several sensor signals on the same circuit board.
lm324.tip: This exhibit uses the TI LM324N. Check both manufacturer and full suffix when ordering or reading specifications. All channels share the supply.
pinNotes: Supply terminals shared by every channel.
steps: Each channel receives an analog signal.
Separate feedback networks set each processing function.
The four outputs feed acquisition circuits or later stages.

lm393.name: LM393P
lm393.subtitle: Dual voltage comparator
lm393.description: Compares the voltages at two inputs and turns a continuously varying voltage into a detectable state. One chip provides two independent threshold-detection channels.
lm393.tip: Open-collector outputs need pull-up resistors to establish a high level. Add hysteresis near the threshold to reduce output chatter.
pinNotes: The two voltage-comparison inputs for each channel.
Pull the output node low or release it so a pull-up resistor establishes a high level.
steps: Apply the sensor voltage and reference voltage to the comparator.
Their relative levels determine the output state.
A controller reads the state to detect threshold crossings.

lm339.name: LM339N
lm339.subtitle: Quad voltage comparator
lm339.description: Contains four voltage comparators to detect whether several signals cross preset thresholds. Common roles include voltage monitoring and state detection.
lm339.tip: Check input common-mode range for the supply conditions. Fit suitable pull-up resistors on each output to interface with downstream logic.
steps: Set a reference threshold for each channel.
Each comparator evaluates its signal relative to the threshold.
Combine the results into a window or multilevel state.

ad620.name: AD620ANZ
ad620.subtitle: Precision instrumentation amplifier
ad620.description: Amplifies tiny voltage differences between two signal wires while suppressing interference common to both. It is often used with bridge sensors.
ad620.tip: High gain also amplifies input errors. Check common-mode voltage, output swing, and the REF potential together.
pinNotes: Inputs for the differential signal being measured.
A resistor between the two gain terminals sets gain.
REF sets the output reference potential and OUT carries the amplified signal.
steps: A bridge sensor produces a small differential voltage.
The instrumentation amplifier scales that difference by the selected gain.
An ADC converts the output into processable digital data.

ina128.name: INA128P
ina128.subtitle: Precision differential measurement front end
ina128.description: An instrumentation amplifier for precision measurement. One external resistor sets its gain to amplify tiny outputs from strain gauges, pressure bridges, and similar sensors.
ina128.tip: Higher gain reduces the allowable differential input amplitude. Choose gain using both the sensor full-scale output and the ADC input range.
pinNotes: Output reference and analog output terminals.
steps: The sensor converts a physical quantity into a differential voltage.
INA128 suppresses common-mode interference and amplifies the differential component.
The acquisition circuit reads the output and applies calibration.

mcp6002.name: MCP6002-I/P
mcp6002.subtitle: Low-voltage dual operational amplifier
mcp6002.description: A dual operational amplifier that works at low supply voltages. Its inputs and outputs can approach both supply rails, supporting analog processing in portable devices.
mcp6002.tip: Rail-to-rail operation allows signals to approach the supply rails. Actual output headroom varies with load, with precise limits given under the datasheet test conditions.
pinNotes: Noninverting and inverting inputs for each channel.
steps: A low-voltage sensor produces an analog signal.
A feedback network controls gain or frequency response.
The output feeds a microcontroller ADC or the next circuit stage.

tl431.name: TL431CLP
tl431.subtitle: Adjustable precision shunt regulator
tl431.description: Stabilizes voltage by adjusting the current flowing through itself. Common uses include supply feedback and voltage references. Its small three-pin body contains a reference and control circuitry.
tl431.tip: TO-92 also houses transistors and other devices, so the complete part number identifies the function. Arrange current limiting and operating current according to the shunt-regulator datasheet.
pinNotes: Feedback reference input for comparing the target voltage.
Lower-potential terminal of the shunt regulator.
steps: A divider feeds the monitored voltage to REF.
Internal circuitry compares feedback with the reference.
Changing cathode current adjusts the feedback state.

lm317.name: LM317T
lm317.subtitle: Adjustable linear regulator
lm317.description: A three-terminal linear regulator whose output voltage is set by external resistors. It illustrates the relationship between feedback, voltage headroom, and heat dissipation.
lm317.tip: Linear-regulator heating depends on the input-output voltage difference and load current. Operating conditions must meet headroom, cooling, and protection requirements together.
pinNotes: Adjustment terminal for the external feedback network.
Connected to OUT. Check insulation requirements when fitting a heatsink.
steps: Divider resistors set the target output.
Internal feedback adjusts the series pass device.
The load receives a stable voltage while energy associated with the voltage drop mainly becomes heat.

lm2596.name: LM2596S-ADJ/NOPB
lm2596.subtitle: Adjustable buck switching regulator
lm2596.description: Uses periodic switching and an external inductor to turn a higher DC voltage into a lower regulated voltage. Common buck modules use this architecture.
lm2596.tip: The chip, inductor, diode, and PCB cooling jointly determine usable load capacity. Interpret module current labels in the context of operating conditions.
pinNotes: Power-switch node. External energy-storage and filtering components form the regulated output.
Reads the divided output voltage for regulation.
steps: The internal switch transfers energy to the inductor each cycle.
The external inductor, capacitor, and diode smooth current flow.
Feedback adjusts switching duty cycle to regulate the output.

mp1584.name: MP1584EN-LF-Z
mp1584.subtitle: Compact adjustable buck converter
mp1584.description: Integrates buck control and a power switch in an eight-pin package. An external inductor, capacitors, and diode form a compact DC supply.
mp1584.tip: The exposed underside pad contributes to heat removal. High-frequency supply performance also depends on PCB layout and inductor and capacitor selection.
pinNotes: Switch node and high-side switch bootstrap terminal.
steps: Input power enters the chip and external energy-storage network.
The power switch controls energy transferred each cycle.
Feedback and compensation maintain a stable output.

tps5430.name: TPS5430DDA
tps5430.subtitle: Wide-input buck converter
tps5430.description: A buck regulator with an integrated power MOSFET. It converts DC from industrial equipment or an adapter into a local power rail.
tps5430.tip: The underside PowerPAD needs a suitable PCB thermal design. Output capability depends jointly on input/output conditions, external components, and temperature rise.
pinNotes: Thermal pad connected as specified in the datasheet.
steps: The internal switch operates at a fixed frequency.
An external inductor and capacitor smooth pulses into DC.
Feedback senses the output and corrects energy transfer.

mt3608.name: MT3608
mt3608.subtitle: Six-pin boost converter
mt3608.description: A tiny six-pin chip controls a boost supply, raising a lower input voltage to a higher output. It is common in portable equipment.
mt3608.tip: The available boosted load current depends on input power, efficiency, and cooling. Peak switch current and output load current describe different circuit locations.
pinNotes: Switch node connected to the external inductor and rectification network.
Detects output voltage through a divider.
steps: The inductor stores energy while the switch conducts.
After switching, the inductor transfers energy to the higher-voltage output.
Feedback regulates the process to keep output near the setpoint.

tp4056.name: TP4056 (ESOP-8)
tp4056.subtitle: Single-cell lithium-battery charge management
tp4056.description: A linear charge-management IC for one series lithium-ion cell. It manages constant-current, constant-voltage, and charge-completion states, and is common on small charger boards.
tp4056.tip: Match battery chemistry and allowed charge voltage to the datasheet. Charging and battery protection have separate responsibilities, and the selected charge current must account for heating.
pinNotes: Input supply, plus battery-voltage sensing and charging connection.
An external resistor sets charging current.
Temperature sensing, enable, and reference ground.
steps: The chip detects battery state and enters the appropriate charging phase.
It first limits current, then regulates voltage near the target voltage.
It reports completion when current falls to the termination condition.

mcp73831.name: MCP73831T-2ACI/OT
mcp73831.subtitle: Five-pin single-cell lithium charger
mcp73831.description: Provides linear charge management for a single lithium-ion or lithium-polymer cell using five pins. It fits compact portable products.
mcp73831.tip: The voltage option in the part number determines the final charging voltage. Check battery specifications, programmed current, and board cooling together.
steps: Detect battery voltage and choose preconditioning or charging.
Manage charging using the programmed current and fixed final voltage.
Update status at completion and monitor recharge conditions.

dw01a.name: DW01A-G
dw01a.subtitle: Single-cell lithium-battery protection controller
dw01a.description: Monitors abnormal voltage and current conditions in one series lithium cell and controls external MOSFETs for protection. It is common on small battery-protection boards.
dw01a.tip: Protection thresholds handle abnormal conditions. A charger matched to the battery sets the normal charge endpoint, while the external MOSFETs also determine protection-board capability.
pinNotes: Detects abnormal current through voltage drop in the external path.
steps: Continuously monitor battery voltage and current-related signals.
Trigger protection after the specified fault delay.
Control external switches and release protection when recovery conditions are met.

xl6019.name: XL6019E1
xl6019.subtitle: Five-pin boost converter
xl6019.description: A boost converter integrating control circuitry and a power switch. An external inductor, diode, and capacitors provide a higher DC output voltage.
xl6019.tip: Output power depends on input conditions, external components, and thermal design. Datasheet switch-current figures describe the capability at the chip switch node.
pinNotes: Switching node for the external energy-storage network.
steps: The inductor stores energy while the switch conducts.
Switching then transfers energy to the output.
Feedback controls duty cycle to stabilize the target voltage.

ir2104.name: IR2104PBF
ir2104.subtitle: Half-bridge gate driver
ir2104.description: Converts controller logic into gate-drive signals for high-side and low-side power devices. It includes interlock and dead-time control.
ir2104.tip: The high-side driver floats relative to VS. Understand the reference relationships of VB, VS, and COM, and verify bootstrap-supply operating conditions in the datasheet.
pinNotes: Gate-drive outputs for high-side and low-side power devices.
High-side floating supply and its reference.
steps: The logic input requests a power-switch state.
Interlock and dead time coordinate both output transitions.
HO and LO charge and discharge the external power-device gates.

uln2003.name: ULN2003AN
uln2003.subtitle: Seven-channel Darlington driver array
uln2003.description: Provides seven transistor-driver channels in one package, allowing logic signals to control relays, indicators, or small stepper-motor windings.
uln2003.tip: Check total chip heating when several channels conduct together. COM is the common terminal of the clamp diodes and must be wired for the load circuit.
pinNotes: Common terminal of the internal clamp diodes.
steps: A logic input controls its Darlington channel.
A conducting channel provides the load-current return path.
The clamp network handles inductive voltage during load switching.

uln2803.name: ULN2803APG
uln2803.subtitle: Eight-channel Darlington driver array
uln2803.description: Provides eight Darlington drivers with input resistors. A group of digital signals controls multiple loads, with integrated clamp diodes.
uln2803.tip: Each channel rating and the total chip thermal limit must both be met. Output on-state voltage drop also affects the voltage delivered to the load.
pinNotes: Common reference for the driver channels.
steps: The controller sends a group of switching signals.
The array converts them into load-current paths.
Check power dissipation and temperature rise for the number of simultaneously active channels.

l293d.name: L293DNE
l293d.subtitle: Dual H-bridge motor driver
l293d.description: Four half-bridge channels form two H bridges to control the direction of two small DC motors, or drive one bipolar stepper motor.
l293d.tip: VCC1 and VCC2 identify the logic and motor supplies. Select loads with motor startup current, output voltage drop, and chip temperature rise in mind.
pinNotes: Logic supply, motor supply, and common ground.
Power outputs connected to motor windings.
Enable the two channel groups separately.
steps: The controller sets the input state of each bridge leg.
The H bridge changes the voltage direction across the motor.
Enable signals and control logic provide start/stop or speed control.

a4988.name: A4988SETTR-T
a4988.subtitle: Microstepping stepper-motor driver
a4988.description: Converts step pulses into controlled current for a two-phase motor. Microstepping support makes it common in desktop manufacturing motion systems.
a4988.tip: Reference voltage and sense resistors set current, subject to cooling limits. Microstepping increases command resolution, while mechanical accuracy also depends on the motor and load.
pinNotes: Motor supply, logic supply, and ground.
Current-limit reference and two-phase current sensing.
steps: The controller sends direction and step pulses.
The internal translator generates the corresponding two-phase current targets.
Chopper regulation controls current so the motor follows the selected step sequence.

tb6612.name: TB6612FNG
tb6612.subtitle: Dual DC-motor driver
tb6612.description: Two motor bridges in a fine-pitch surface-mount package independently control direction, speed, braking, and standby for two DC motors.
tb6612.tip: Operating current varies with motor supply, PWM conditions, and temperature rise. Use recommended operating conditions and check motor stall current when selecting the load.
pinNotes: Motor supply, logic supply, and ground.
Direction and state control for both motors.
Power outputs for the two motors.
steps: Direction inputs determine each bridge state.
PWM adjusts the fraction of time the motor receives energy.
Standby and braking controls complete motion management.

ads1115.name: ADS1115IDGSR
ads1115.subtitle: 16-bit I²C analog-to-digital converter
ads1115.description: Converts analog voltages into digital readings, with an integrated input multiplexer and programmable gain. It suits slowly changing signals such as temperature and pressure.
ads1115.tip: PGA range settings and permitted pin voltage have separate constraints. Actual input voltage must meet supply-rail and common-mode requirements.
pinNotes: Address selection and threshold-alert or conversion-ready signal.
steps: The controller selects input channel, gain, and data rate.
The ADC converts the chosen analog voltage into a digital code.
Read the result over I²C and scale it using the selected range.

mcp4725.name: MCP4725A0T-E/CH
mcp4725.subtitle: 12-bit I²C digital-to-analog converter
mcp4725.description: Converts numbers sent by a controller into an analog voltage. Integrated EEPROM can retain the output setting to restore at power-up.
mcp4725.tip: Use the volatile register for continuous waveform updates. EEPROM stores settings that must survive power loss, with write endurance considered.
steps: The controller converts the target voltage into a digital code.
Write the code to the conversion register over I²C.
The DAC produces the voltage and stores the power-up setting when requested.

pcf8591.name: PCF8591P
pcf8591.subtitle: 8-bit ADC / DAC
pcf8591.description: Combines acquisition of four analog inputs with one analog output, communicating over I²C. It offers a direct introduction to ADC and DAC operation.
pcf8591.tip: An 8-bit converter provides 256 digital codes. Actual measurement accuracy also depends on reference voltage, noise, and conversion errors.
pinNotes: Select the device address on the bus.
steps: The controller selects input mode and acquisition channel.
The ADC converts the analog input into a digital reading.
Writing DAC data produces the corresponding analog output.

lm386.name: LM386N-1/NOPB
lm386.subtitle: Low-voltage audio power amplifier
lm386.description: Amplifies a small audio signal to power a small loudspeaker. Its internally set basic gain makes it a classic low-power audio IC.
lm386.tip: The part suffix affects supply and output capability. Watch clipping as volume rises, and interpret output power with its load and distortion conditions.
pinNotes: Audio output and internal-bias bypass terminal.
steps: The audio source supplies a small AC signal.
The internal amplifier applies the selected gain.
The output stage supplies load current to produce sound from the speaker.

tda2030.name: TDA2030AV
tda2030.subtitle: Classic class-AB audio power amplifier
tda2030.description: A classic mono audio amplifier in a five-pin power package. External feedback and a heatsink help it drive a speaker and illustrate power-stage thermal design.
tda2030.tip: Datasheet power figures include supply, load, and distortion conditions. Check the electrical potential and insulation method of the metal thermal area in the device documentation.
pinNotes: Noninverting and inverting inputs. The feedback network connects to the inverting input.
steps: The input and feedback signals are compared at the amplifier front end.
The class-AB output stage supplies current in both directions to the speaker.
The thermal structure removes dissipated heat to maintain an allowed junction temperature.

pam8403.name: PAM8403DR
pam8403.subtitle: Stereo class-D audio amplifier
pam8403.description: Converts left and right audio into fast switching outputs that drive small speakers. Its class-D architecture suits low-voltage portable audio equipment.
pam8403.tip: Both terminals of each speaker are driven by the amplifier. Use a measurement method suited to bridge outputs, and interpret power ratings with supply, impedance, and distortion conditions.
pinNotes: Analog and power supplies and grounds.
steps: Two audio channels enter the internal modulator.
The power stage drives outputs through rapid switching.
The speakers respond to the audio component and produce left and right sound.
